inventory.reason: New round-2 test. The whole `/sign in again/i` guard block deleted (useMfaEnrollment.ts:84-86); the hook surfaced 'Could not start MFA enrollment: Please sign in again to continue.' and the test FAILED. The guard is really the thing under test.

inventory.test: does not surface provider text that would trigger the step-up link
inventory.reason: PROVEN equivalent, not merely unkilled. The guard's subject swapped from the composed `text` to the raw `message` (useMfaEnrollment.ts:84); the test passed. Proof for ALL inputs, not just this fixture: text === 'Could not start MFA enrollment: ' + message, the pattern /sign in again/i is unanchored, and a match can therefore differ only if it straddles the seam — which requires some non-empty prefix of 'sign in again' ('s','si','sig','sign','sign ',...) to be a suffix of 'Could not start MFA enrollment: '. That prefix ends in ': ', and no prefix of 'sign in again' ends in ':' or is ' '. No straddling match exists, so the two subjects agree on every message. A claim about the MUTANT, so it does not block.

findings.title: The promised invariant test cannot falsify its invariant: `fc.string()` never draws a name in the RepWorth sequence, so a `return 'RepWorth'` implementation passes it
findings.arbiter_reasoning: CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT (rt2-1149-01). The fix biases the arbitrary toward the sequence itself (mfa.test.ts:192-199: fc.oneof over fc.constantFrom('RepWorth','RepWorth 2'..'RepWorth 5'), fc.string(), fc.constant(null)). Re-running the round-1 survivor M4a — `nextFactorFriendlyName` body replaced by `void existingNames; return 'RepWorth';` — against the SAME test title now exits 1 with exactly one executed test, where round 1 recorded a pass over 100,000 draws. The shape of the fix also matches the house-style reference the intake names (src/lib/reviews/__tests__/sentiment.test.ts:46), which draws from the real domain. Round-2 additionally confirms the new second property is not the load-bearing one for this mutant (see RT-1149-F5) — property 1 alone kills it.

findings.title: Provider-controlled enrollment error text now reaches `isStepUpRequiredError`'s /sign in again/i sniff, which can attach a 'Verify with your authenticator' link to an enrollment failure
findings.reason: CLOSED AT THE HOOK. `enrollmentErrorMessage` now falls back to the generic sentence when the composed text matches the consumer's pattern (useMfaEnrollment.ts:84-86), and the guard is pinned in both directions: deleting it reddens the new test (rt2-1149-05) and inverting it reddens the pre-existing unmapped-error test (rt2-1149-07). Re-verified that this was the ONLY exposure: a recorded search for sentence-sniffing classifiers over UI error strings (`rg -n "test\((error|err|message|text)\)" src/app src/components --glob '!**/__tests__/**'`) returns exactly two sites, this one and SecuritySections.tsx:42, and every other error string the hook can dispatch is a fixed constant (useMfaEnrollment.ts:181, :246, :252, :265, :271, :288, :293, :299) of which only the unenroll-403 hint at :288 matches the pattern — which is the one case that SHOULD keep the link. The residual duplicated-regex drift risk is carried forward as RT-1149-F3 rather than left inside a closed finding.

findings.title: Two independent copies of `/sign in again/i` with nothing binding them, and the new test asserts the exact copy string rather than the consumer's predicate
findings.reason: The fix works by duplicating the consumer's pattern into the hook (the comment at :77-83 justifies this by the ESLint ban on `@/app/**` imports from `src/components/**`, eslint.config.mjs:172-178 — verified true for PRODUCTION code). But nothing fails if the two copies diverge: widen SecuritySections.tsx:42 to, say, /sign in again|re-authenticate/i and every test in the repo stays green while the enrollment path re-acquires the exact defect RT-1149-F2 described. The new test (useMfaEnrollment.test.tsx:256-273) asserts `toBe('Could not start MFA enrollment.')` — an exact copy string standing in for 'this sentence does not trigger the step-up link', which is the real contract. Behavioural replacement, and it is cheap: the ESLint ban EXEMPTS tests (eslint.config.mjs:178 and :251 both ignore `**/__tests__/**`) and the repo already does exactly this (src/components/approval/__tests__/approval-client.test.tsx:9 imports from `@/app/api/...`), so the test can `import { isStepUpRequiredError } from '@/app/(authenticated)/settings/security/SecuritySections'` and assert `expect(isStepUpRequiredError(result.current.error)).toBe(false)`. That binds the two copies at the one place they must agree. P2: a latent drift risk over a UI affordance, not a defect at HEAD — rt2-1149-13 confirms the patterns are byte-identical today.

findings.title: The rewritten `mfa.ts` directory row re-asserts `src/proxy.ts` `:92-103` for the inlined lenient AAL read; at HEAD those lines are the admin CORS preflight
findings.reason: Re-resolved against HEAD e9cdaa2b. The row says: '`src/proxy.ts` skips these, inlining its lenient read (`:92-103`, ADR 0025 D6)'. src/proxy.ts:92-103 is `adminCorsPreflight` — 'ADR 0026 D3's allowlisted column', a 204 preflight builder with no AAL read in it. The actual inlined lenient read is `getAalGate` at src/proxy.ts:260-271 (`getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel()` at :264, the `nextLevel === 'aal2' && currentLevel !== 'aal2'` lenient test at :268). The ADR half of the citation IS true: ADR 0025's decision 6 (docs/adr/0025-dual-mode-admin-gate.md:123-126) is the `src/proxy.ts` branch-4 decision and names 'the lenient/strict AAL disagreement already in the tree'. So the defect is confined to the line span. The span was carried over verbatim from the pre-fix row, but this diff REWROTE that sentence, so it is a claim this round re-asserted. A stale line number is a P1 by the skill's own rule, not a P0 — the row is misleading about WHERE, not about WHAT. Fix: `:260-271`. NOTE ON METHOD: `prevalidate-plan.py` was present and ran, but reported 'CITATIONS: 0 checked, 0 unresolved' on this file — its citation grammar does not recognise the row's bare '(`:92-103`, ...)' form — so this was found by hand-resolution, and no part of this doc's claims rests on that script's PASS.

findings.title: The new second property is vacuous exactly when the result is the unnumbered `RepWorth`, so it carries no weight alone for that case
findings.reason: Static, no launch needed. The property matches the result, derives `n`, and then asserts only that every SMALLER name in the sequence is taken: `for (let i = 1; i < n; i += 1)` (mfa.test.ts:220-223). When the result is 'RepWorth', n === 1 and the loop body never executes, so the whole property reduces to 'the result matches /^RepWorth(?: (\d+))?$/'. That is why the round-1 survivor `return 'RepWorth';` would pass THIS property on every draw — it is property 1 (rt2-1149-01), not property 2, that closes RT-1149-F1. Reported as P2 rather than a confirmed survivor precisely because the pairing is deliberate and sound: property 1 owns non-collision and property 2 owns minimality, and together they pin first-unused. It is recorded because the title claims the stronger thing on its own. Behavioural strengthening, one line: add `expect(taken.has(next)).toBe(false);` inside property 2 so the test's own title is true without leaning on its sibling. Round-2 did confirm property 2 is not dead weight — rt2-1149-02 shows it kills the gap-fill-to-append mutant that property 1 cannot see.
